problem: Transformer VLN agents such as HAMT and RecBERT decide from the instruction plus past and current observations only. They never explicitly estimate where the final goal lies in unexplored space. They also encode history either as a flat sequence or through separate, complex GNN map modules, so they cannot plan globally over the explored topology.
motivation: A human reading an instruction like 'exit the bedroom ... stop at the end of the hallway' imagines a rough destination before moving and refines it along the way. That guess about the 'future' guides long-horizon planning. Existing agents model only the present and the past, and layout-aware agents such as SSM rely on heavy graph networks. The paper argues that goal imagination and topology can both be built directly into a single cross-modal transformer.
key_idea: Add learnable 'imaginary' target tokens for the cells of a fixed grid over the unexplored area and add topology-masked, position-embedded history tokens, both inside one HAMT-style transformer. The agent refines a long-term target estimate at every step and can choose any visited node as an action, which enables target-driven global planning with backtracking.
insight: In the Table 3 ablation on R2R val-unseen, each component adds a modest gain in SR. The structured transformer (relative-position embeddings plus an adjacency attention mask) gives the largest unseen gain, 65.7→67.7 SR, though val-seen SR drops (75.0→73.7). The global action space mainly helps val-seen SR (73.7→77.1) and adds 0.8 SR unseen, while unseen SPL slips slightly (62.5→62.4) because backtracking lengthens paths. The IST target tokens add +1.2 SR and +0.3 SPL (68.5→69.7 / 62.4→62.7). Grid design matters: 5×5 cells at 6 m spacing works best, while 7×7 hurts (SPL 60.8), so targets that are too dense or too many add noise. Target-estimation error falls both as an episode progresses and over training as SR rises, so the agent really does learn to refine its guess of the goal.
method: Structured Transformer: each visited node becomes a history token h_t = f_V(panorama) + f_A(heading/elevation sin/cos) + f_T(t) + f_P(relative (x,y) location from start). The history-to-history block of the attention mask is multiplied elementwise by the nav-graph adjacency matrix, so information flows only along explored edges.

Token set: at each step five token types enter one cross-modal transformer (HAMT architecture and hyper-parameters): a global token (initialized as the BERT sentence embedding x_0), BERT instruction tokens (fixed over time), q target tokens, t-1 history tokens and 36 view tokens. View tokens of navigable directions also receive f_P positional embeddings of the locations they lead to.

Global Action Space: the action set is the k^t navigable view tokens plus all previously visited history tokens (a 'jump' back or backtrack). A history token and a view token pointing to the same viewpoint count as different actions. Policy = softmax(MLP(token ⊙ global token)).

Imaginary Scene Tokenization (IST): a d×d grid (d=5, spacing s=6 m) centered at the start position. Each cell center is a target token initialized as f_P(l_i) ⊙ x_0 and updated through the transformer every step. MLP + softmax over (c_i ⊙ g^t) predicts which cell contains the destination.

Training: alternate teacher forcing (L = 0.2·IL + 0.1·target loss) and student forcing (L = 1·RL (A2C-style as in HAMT) + 0.4·history-teacher loss + 0.1·target loss). The history-teacher loss supervises the global-action-space action on the GT trajectory closest to the goal; the target loss is cross-entropy to the grid cell nearest the goal. Initialized from HAMT, 100k iterations, batch 8, lr 1e-5, Adam, 1 V100.
REVERIE grounding: navigation by TD-STP; object selection at the stop location by a separate ViLBERT fine-tuned on the REVERIE training set.

setting.backbone: HAMT-style cross-modal transformer (BERT instruction encoder + HAMT panoramic ViT-feature encoder), initialized from HAMT and fine-tuned; separate fine-tuned ViLBERT for REVERIE object grounding
setting.training_data: R2R training split (and REVERIE training split for REVERIE), trained with IL+RL for 100k iterations; weights initialized from the HAMT checkpoint (whose pre-training is inherited, not redone here); no additional augmentation data stated
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discretized views) plus agent heading/elevation and relative (x,y) positions of visited and neighbouring viewpoints from the nav graph
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints: currently navigable neighbours plus any previously visited viewpoint (global action space with jump/backtrack), plus stop
setting.privileged: none beyond the standard R2R/REVERIE pre-defined nav graph (navigability, viewpoint coordinates used for positional embeddings, ability to jump to visited nodes)

numbers_note: Table 1 prints R2R results as integers (except NE); the ablation Table 3 row #3 (full model) gives one-decimal values for val-seen (77.0/72.5/2.34/82.9) and val-unseen (69.7/62.7/3.22/76.3). TL is not reported. The text contains a typo ('SR from 58.5% to 69.7%' should be 68.5→69.7). Table 1 lists HAMT val-unseen NE as 2.29 (bolded), which looks like a typo: the paper's own HAMT baseline in Table 3 has NE 3.65. Target-estimation-error analyses appear only in figures.
results: On R2R, TD-STP reaches 70 SR / 63 SPL on val-unseen and 67 SR / 61 SPL / 3.73 NE on test-unseen, beating the prior SOTA HAMT (66/61 and 65/60). On REVERIE test-unseen it reaches 35.89 SR / 27.51 SPL / 19.88 RGS / 15.40 RGSPL, versus the best prior SR of 30.80 (SIA) and HAMT's 30.40 SR / 26.67 SPL, a 16.5% relative SR gain. On REVERIE val-unseen, however, its SPL (27.32) and RGSPL (16.56) trail HAMT (30.20 / 17.28).
limitations: Relies on the pre-defined discrete nav graph (stated by the authors), including teleport-like jumps back to visited nodes; SLAM-based online mapping is left to future work.
Fixed-size grid centered at the start (5×5 cells, 6 m spacing) is hand-tuned and sensitive (7×7 or 4/8/10 m spacing hurt), and may not cover larger scenes.
Gains over HAMT are modest (IST alone +1.2 SR on val-unseen); on REVERIE val-unseen, SPL/RGSPL fall below HAMT, and grounding uses a separate off-the-shelf ViLBERT.
